title: Fire safety and liveability under higher occupancy caps for private homes
asked: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo asked whether URA has assessed fire safety and evacuation risks from the temporary relaxation of the occupancy cap for private residences, and what safeguards address higher turnover and foot traffic from the increased cap.
response: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi said all residential premises are subject to SCDF fire safety requirements, including ventilated escape routes, exit staircases and fire compartments, and that these standards remain sufficient under the temporary higher occupancy cap for larger private residential properties. He said the higher cap applies only to larger private properties, at least 90 square kilometres, equivalent to a typical four-room HDB flat, and owners must register with URA and pay $20. Monitoring of common spaces and corridors falls to the MCST, alongside SCDF public education, safety and security days, block evacuation drills, and inspections when hazards are highlighted.
